newsitem.title: FRANCE: France concerned about Lebanon clashes.
newsitem.headline: France concerned about Lebanon clashes.

text.p: France expressed concern on Friday about an escalation of violence between Moslem guerrillas and Israel in south Lebanon and said Israeli forces had also opened fire on U.N. peacekeepers.
"Incidents have multiplied in the zone occupied by Israel as have Israeli reprisal bombings and the firing of rockets into Israel proper from Lebanon," ministry spokesman jacques Rummelhardt said.
"All the parties must show restraint," he said, adding that "UNIFIL (U.N. peacekeeping) troops were fired on by the Israeli army" in an incident on Thursday in which there were no casualties.

In Jerusalem, an Israeli army spokesman denied Israeli forces had fired on the U.N. soldiers. "The Israeli army informed the United Nations that the area is not quiet and asked the U.N.to leave the area for the security of the peacekeepers. The army in no instance fired at U.N.forces," he told Reuters.
Another French official said there were reports that the incident occurred when Finnish troops sought to recover the bodies of three Lebanese guerrillas killed in a clash with Israeli troops.
Rummelhardt also said France condemned two late night bomb attacks in Tel Aviv on Thursday.
"Violence and fanaticism have already struck Israel as they have struck other peoples of the area, but they will not halt the advance of peoples of the area towards peace," he said.
